recommendation_1: Replace the single linear layer in Net with a Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) architecture consisting of two hidden layers with 128 and 64 neurons respectively, using ReLU activation functions.
rationale_1: The current model is a linear classifier which lacks the capacity to capture non-linear relationships in the image data; adding hidden layers allows the model to learn hierarchical feature representations.
recommendation_4: Add nn.Dropout(0.2) after the hidden layers in the Net architecture.
rationale_4: Dropout acts as a regularization technique that prevents overfitting by randomly zeroing activations, forcing the network to learn more robust features, which helps when client data distribution varies.
recommendation_5: Replace F.log_softmax and nn.CrossEntropyLoss with a combination of nn.Linear output (raw logits) and nn.CrossEntropyLoss, while experimenting with the Adam optimizer instead of SGD.
rationale_5: Adam optimizer typically converges faster than SGD due to adaptive learning rates per parameter, which can be more efficient in federated settings where local communication rounds are limited.
recommendation_6: Change the activation function from ReLU to LeakyReLU(0.1) or ELU in the hidden layers of the Net class.
rationale_6: LeakyReLU or ELU prevents the 'dying ReLU' problem by allowing a small gradient for negative inputs, ensuring that more neurons remain active during the training process across different clients.
